docs.title: zxcv
docs.text: A minimalist, fast .tool-versions manager. It is a cleaner, friendlier alternative to asdf that plugs into its plugin ecosystem with a highly minimalistic command surface and enjoyably better performance.

docs.title: Why zxcv?
docs.text:
• Dead simple: Handful of self-explanatory commands.
  • No plugins: No manual plugin management, we do it all for you.
  • Faster installs: Quick setups so you can have your tools ready ASAP.
  • .tool-definitions: A new declarative way to define custom tools.
  • Cleanest DX: See it for yourself!

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://snehil-shah.github.io/zxcv/install.sh | sh

Then in any project with a .tool-versions file:

zxcv install

That's it.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This page walks through your first install with zxcv. Assumes you've already installed zxcv.

docs.title: Installing tools from .tool-versions
docs.text:
zxcv reads the standard asdf .tool-versions format. Drop a file like this in your project:

nodejs 20.11.0
python 3.11.5
ruby 3.2.0

Then:

zxcv install

docs.title: Installing a single tool
docs.text:
zxcv install nodejs 20.11.0
zxcv install python latest
zxcv install golang latest:1.26

By default this also pins the version into your local .tool-versions. Use --no-save to install without pinning, or --global to write to $HOME/.tool-versions instead.

docs.title: Discovering available tools and versions you can install
docs.text:
zxcv search node          # tools matching "node"
zxcv search nodejs latest # latest stable version of nodejs
zxcv search nodejs 20     # all nodejs versions starting with "20"

docs.title: Running installed binaries
docs.text:
Once installed, the binaries are on your PATH. Just use them directly:

node --version
python --version

Tip

If you are confused on what all tools are resolved for your directory, run the zxcv current command.

To inspect which version our binary resolves to:

zxcv which node

To run a binary at a specific version without changing the active version:

zxcv exec nodejs 18.19.0 -- node script.js

docs.title: Quick install
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://snehil-shah.github.io/zxcv/install.sh | sh

This downloads the latest release for your OS/architecture and also modifies you shell rc (see customization below if you wish to avoid this).

After install, restart your shell or source your rc file.

docs.title: Pinning a version
docs.text:
# Positional argument:
curl -fsSL https://snehil-shah.github.io/zxcv/install.sh | sh -s v0.1.0

# Or via environment variable:
ZXCV_VERSION=v0.1.0 curl -fsSL https://snehil-shah.github.io/zxcv/install.sh | sh

The v prefix is auto-added if you forget it (0.1.0 works the same).

docs.title: Customizing installation
docs.text:
Set environment variables before running the script:

Variable Default Effect ZXCV_VERSION (latest) Pin a specific release tag. ZXCV_INSTALL_DIR ~/.local/bin Where to place the zxcv binary. ZXCV_NO_MODIFY_RC (unset) If 1, skip shell rc file modifications (PATH + completions).

docs.title: Uninstalling
docs.text: curl -fsSL https://snehil-shah.github.io/zxcv/uninstall.sh | sh

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
• macOS (arm64, amd64)
  • Linux (arm64, amd64)

Windows is not supported. WSL works since it presents as Linux.

docs.title: zxcv
docs.text: zxcv - A minimalist, fast .tool-versions manager

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text:
zxcv is a dead simple tool-version manager — a cleaner, friendlier alternative to asdf that plugs into its ecosystem with a highly minimalistic command surface and enjoyably better performance.

Usage:

zxcv [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [command [COMMAND OPTIONS]] [ARGUMENTS...]

docs.title: current
docs.text:
Show resolved tools and their versions for the current directory

--version: output version(s) only

docs.title: search
docs.text: Search the upstream tool registry by tool name, or a tool's available versions

docs.title: install
docs.text:
Install resolved tools or add new ones

--global: install globally; affects the global ~/.tool-versions file

--no-save: do not modify any .tool-versions file

docs.title: exec
docs.text: Run a specific binary

docs.title: which
docs.text: Output the resolved path of a tool's binary

docs.title: list
docs.text: List installed tools and their versions

docs.title: uninstall
docs.text: Remove installed tools

docs.title: current
docs.text: current - Show resolved tools and their versions for the current directory

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text:
Shows all active tools (with version and source) for the current working directory by resolving all applicable .tool-versions files and global installations. If a specific tool is provided, prints only its resolution.

Usage:

current [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [command [COMMAND OPTIONS]] [ARGUMENTS...]

docs.title: GLOBAL OPTIONS
docs.text: --version: output version(s) only

docs.title: exec
docs.text: exec - Run a specific binary

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text:
Runs the binary under a specified tool and version. If no version is specified for the tool, it defaults to the resolved version for the current working directory.

Usage:

exec [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [command [COMMAND OPTIONS]] [ARGUMENTS...]

docs.title: install
docs.text: install - Install resolved tools or add new ones

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text:
Downloads & installs all resolved tools for the current directory, if no arguments are provided. If a specific tool and its version are provided, it installs only that and adds them to the local .tool-versions manifest. This behavior can be controlled to save it to the global manifest or not save at all using the --global and --no-save flags, respectively. You can specify the version as 'latest' (or with a prefix 'latest:') to simply install and pin the latest version of the tool.

Usage:

install [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [command [COMMAND OPTIONS]] [ARGUMENTS...]

docs.title: GLOBAL OPTIONS
docs.text:
--global: install globally; affects the global ~/.tool-versions file

--no-save: do not modify any .tool-versions file

docs.title: list
docs.text: list - List installed tools and their versions

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text:
Lists all the installed tools and their versions. Pass a tool name to see installed versions for a specific tool.

Usage:

list [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [command [COMMAND OPTIONS]] [ARGUMENTS...]

docs.title: search
docs.text: search - Search the upstream tool registry by tool name, or a tool's available versions

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text:
Quickly finds the tools or a tool's available versions you want by name. You can use this to discover if a tool exists and by what name, or finding the right version to pin it to.

Usage:

search [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [command [COMMAND OPTIONS]] [ARGUMENTS...]

docs.title: uninstall
docs.text: uninstall - Remove installed tools

docs.title: DESCRIPTION
docs.text:
Uninstalls tools previously installed by zxcv. With no arguments, removes all tools. With a tool name, removes all versions of that tool. With a tool name and version, removes just that version.

Usage:

uninstall [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [command [COMMAND OPTIONS]] [ARGUMENTS...]

docs.title: which
docs.text: which - Output the resolved path of a tool's binary

docs.title: SYNOPSIS
docs.text:
which

Usage:

which [GLOBAL OPTIONS] [command [COMMAND OPTIONS]] [ARGUMENTS...]

docs.title: .tool-definitions
docs.text:
Drop a .tool-definitions file alongside your .tool-versions to override or extend the upstream tools registry, for tools that aren't in the registry.

This is what a .tool-definitions file looks like:

internal-cli https://github.com/our-org/asdf-internal-cli.git
my-fork-of-nodejs git@github.com:me/asdf-nodejs-fork.git
my-plugin ./vendor/my-plugin

Each line is <tool> <source>. The source can be a git:// or https:// URL, an SSH-style git URL, or a filesystem path (absolute, or relative to the .tool-definitions file).

You can also include comments:

# Internal tools
internal-cli https://github.com/our-org/asdf-internal-cli.git
# This is another comment
my-plugin ./vendor/my-plugin

Tip

Filesystem paths are symlinked instead of cloned. Handy when authoring plugins — edit your local checkout in place and re-install to see changes.

docs.title: .tool-versions
docs.text:
Whenever a .tool-versions file is present in a directory, the tool versions it declares will be used in that directory and any subdirectories.

This is what a .tool-versions file looks like:

ruby 2.5.3
nodejs 10.15.0

You can also include comments:

ruby 2.5.3 # This is a comment
# This is another comment
nodejs 10.15.0

Tip

Use the search command to find the exact tool names and versions you wish to use.

You can specify system in place of the version if you wish to use the system installed binary instead of zxcv managed ones.

Note

The entire asdf-spec is not supported. Only a simpler version of it defined above.
